clue.text: A little girl to work for the country (once so called)

parts.note: Sal is a short pet form of the girl's name Sally or Sarah
op is the usual abbreviation of opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone sends a young girl off to work for her nation.
explanation.walkthrough: SALOP was long the official name of the English county of Shropshire (1974-80) and its old abbreviation; 'country' is used loosely for that county.
explanation.definitionFit: Salop is the former official name of Shropshire, an English county in the West Midlands region.

clue.text: Brief salutation by radio

parts.note: brief means short
a wave is a greeting with the hand

explanation.surface: A quick hello sent over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortwave is a band of radio frequencies used for long-distance broadcasting.

clue.text: Dwelling 10 is free to occupy

definitions.meaning: a small house, such as a gatekeeper's
10 across is a mason; Freemasons meet in their own meeting place

explanation.surface: A home that a builder may move into without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a small house, and a Masonic lodge is where Freemasons meet.

clue.text: When these senior housemen show a narrow outlook?

definitions.text: When these senior housemen show a narrow outlook?

parts.words: When these senior housemen show a narrow outlook?
parts.note: members of the House of Lords, read as an era of squinting: to peer is to look narrowly

explanation.surface: A question about when hospital doctors become narrow-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers sit in the House of Lords; split, the word suggests an age of peering, looking narrowly.

clue.text: Like a sauna (south of France opening detailed)

parts.note: sud is the French word for south

indicators.note: de-tailed: the word has its tail, its last letter, cut off

parts.note: an orifice is an opening

explanation.surface: A sauna is described by its location in the south of France, in some detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as 'described fully' but means 'lose its tail', so ORIFICE drops its final E to give ORIFIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudorific means causing sweat, which is exactly what a sauna is for.

clue.text: Models changed infrequently

indicators.note: the letters of the word are changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: Fashion models are rarely replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom means rarely, not often.

clue.text: Some ladies do put on bets

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece is placed on top of the other

parts.note: taken as written
wagers are bets

explanation.surface: Some women like to place bets.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'do put on bets' as placing wagers; in a down clue 'put on' means one piece is stacked above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowagers are widows holding titles from their late husbands, a class of grand women.

clue.text: Wild behaviour of a member in great anger

indicators.note: the article and member are placed inside the word for great anger

parts.note: rage is great anger
MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP behaves wildly in a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a spell of violent, uncontrolled behaviour.

clue.text: Cast a fine new spell

indicators.note: new signals that the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A witch casts a fresh enchantment.
explanation.definitionFit: To fascinate is to bewitch, as if casting a charm.

clue.text: Nancy can be so knowing

indicators.note: the name can be turned into another word by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A girl called Nancy is perceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd or astute.

clue.text: Strange member of society — not even a don!

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd
a university don is often a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: An eccentric person in society who is not even an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows are a friendly society, so one of its members is an oddfellow; 'Strange' teases that such a member is odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddfellows are members of a fraternal friendly society, hence 'member of society', with 'Strange' as a nod to the odd part.

clue.text: Four feathers from one on the square?

definitions.meaning: the author from whom the novel The Four Feathers came
Freemasons are said to act 'on the square', honestly, after their square emblem

explanation.surface: Four feathers are plucked from someone who is honest.
explanation.definitionFit: A.E.W. Mason wrote the novel The Four Feathers, and a Freemason's emblem is the square.

clue.text: Legislation forbidding fun and games seemingly

definitions.text: Legislation forbidding fun and games seemingly

parts.words: Legislation forbidding fun and games seemingly
parts.note: the physics principle of attraction, read as a statute demanding seriousness and solemnity

explanation.surface: A killjoy statute bans all amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravity also means solemnity, so a law of gravity sounds like a rule against frivolity, though it is the physics principle.

clue.text: He takes a bow before his performance

definitions.text: He takes a bow before his performance

parts.words: He takes a bow before his performance
parts.note: an actor bows after a show, but this person picks up a longbow before he shoots

explanation.surface: A performer bows before going on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowman picks up his bow before he shoots, not to acknowledge applause.

clue.text: Eccentric letter

explanation.definitionFit: A character is an odd person, and also a written symbol such as an alphabet sign.

clue.text: Carte blanche for such drawing?

definitions.meaning: full freedom to act as one sees fit
sketching done without ruler or compasses

explanation.surface: Being given full licence to draw however you like.
explanation.definitionFit: A free hand means complete discretion, and freehand drawing is done without instruments.

clue.text: Flowers of the underworld bring great misfortunes

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and the underworld itself
asters are daisy-like flowers

explanation.surface: Blooms from Hades bring catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Disasters are calamities, great misfortunes.

clue.text: Extremely backward, what parents of largest families do

definitions.text: what parents of largest families do
definitions.meaning: parents who raise the most children ...

explanation.surface: Parents of huge families are very behind the times.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearmost means at the very back; split, rear most describes bringing up the most children.

clue.text: Ploughing is one of his activities

definitions.text: Ploughing is one of his activities

parts.words: Ploughing is one of his activities
parts.note: plough is British slang for failing a candidate, which this marker of papers does

explanation.surface: A farmer lists ploughing among his jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plough' in old British university slang means to fail a candidate in an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets and marks tests may fail, or plough, candidates.

clue.text: Concentrated in verbal form

parts.note: a tense is a form of a verb showing time

explanation.surface: Focused on the forms of verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means concentrated, strong or focused.

clue.text: .All hands on board to the propellers

indicators.note: on board a ship means within it, so the ship's letters go round the crew

parts.note: the ship you go on board, a steamship, SS
all hands means the whole crew of a ship

explanation.surface: A call for the entire crew to go to the ship's propellers.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's screws are its propellers, the bladed shafts that drive it.

clue.text: His is often a paying job

definitions.text: His is often a paying job

parts.words: His is often a paying job
parts.note: a paying job usually means well rewarded, but here it is the bank clerk whose work is paying money out

explanation.surface: His work is usually well rewarded.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank teller's work is literally paying out money.

clue.text: One who refuses to be measured for stockings?

definitions.meaning: the unit for the fineness of yarn in hosiery

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to be measured for new stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A denier is one who denies, and denier is the unit of yarn fineness in stockings.

clue.text: Justice tempered with mercy in this old court?

definitions.text: Justice tempered with mercy in this old court?

parts.words: Justice tempered with mercy in this old court?
parts.note: quarter means mercy shown to a foe, so sittings of this court sound like merciful sessions

explanation.surface: An old court is praised for blending fairness with clemency.
explanation.walkthrough: These were English county courts sitting four times a year, abolished in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarter means clemency, so sittings giving quarter suggest mercy, while the term names the old periodic county courts.

clue.text: Opening measure of 22ac

indicators.note: only the opening part of the referenced answer is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: the answer to 22 across, the old court

explanation.surface: The first measure of a court session.
explanation.definitionFit: A quart is a measure of liquid, two pints.

clue.text: Eisteddfodic graduate — something of an egghead?

definitions.meaning: one of the grades of the Welsh bardic order at the Eisteddfod

explanation.surface: A Welsh festival bard is a bit of an intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eisteddfod is the Welsh festival of poetry and music; its bardic order has ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovate is a rank in the Welsh bardic order, and ovate means egg-shaped.

clue.text: Anne Brontë's alias in London

definitions.meaning: the pen name, with the surname Bell, under which the youngest Brontë sister published

explanation.surface: Anne Brontë used a pen name while in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Brontë's pen name was Acton Bell, and Acton is also a west London district.

clue.text: Start to speak about one enemy of sobriety

indicators.note: the word for speaking goes round the other pieces, surrounding them

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally
I is the Roman numeral one
gin, a spirit, is an enemy of staying sober

explanation.surface: Someone begins a speech against a foe of temperance.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or set something in motion.

clue.text: One very cruel to men in high places

indicators.note: the men are set inside the high places, placed between them

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill; two of them for the plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tyrant treats the men at the top harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor inflicts suffering, someone cruel.

clue.text: Dances unsteadily

parts.note: lively Scottish dances, or the verb for staggering about

explanation.surface: Someone dances in a wobbly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Reels are Scottish dances, and to reel is to stagger, so the word covers both readings.
